content_html:
Cusco is an incredible destination that combines history, nature and culture. Depending on how much time you have and your budget, you can tailor your trip to make the most of it. Here we show you three ideal itineraries depending on the length of your stay.

Itinerary for 3 days: The essentials of Cusco

Ideal for: Travelers with little time who want to know the essentials.

Day 1: Historical and cultural Cusco

  • Plaza de Armas and Cathedral.
  • Temple of Qoricancha.
  • Sacsayhuamán, Q’enqo, Puka Pukara and Tambomachay.
  • San Pedro Market to try typical food.

Day 2: Sacred Valley

  • Early departure to Pisac (market and ruins).
  • Lunch at Urubamba.
  • Visit to Ollantaytambo (ruins and town).
  • Train to Aguas Calientes.

Day 3: Machu Picchu

  • Visit to Machu Picchu early in the morning.
  • Option to upload to Huayna Picchu or the Machu Picchu Mountain.
  • Return to Cusco in the afternoon/evening.

5-Day Itinerary: Exploring Further

Ideal for: Travelers with more time who want to know beyond the essentials.

Days 1 and 2: Same as the 3-day itinerary.
Day 3: Machu Picchu, but with the option of staying in Aguas Calientes an extra night for greater comfort.


Day 4: Maras, Moray and Chinchero

  • salt mines Maras.
  • circular platforms Moray.
  • artisanal village of Chinchero.
  • Return to Cusco to enjoy the nightlife (bars or clubs).

Day 5: Vinicunca or Palcoyo (Colored Mountains)

  • Full day excursion to the Mountain of 7 Colors or the least demanding Palcoyo.
  • Return to Cusco and farewell.

7-day itinerary: The complete experience

Ideal for: Those who want to explore Cusco in depth.

Days 1 to 5: Same as the 5-day itinerary.
Day 6: Humantay Lagoon

  • 1.5 hour walk to the lagoon.
  • Free time for photos and connection with nature.
  • Return to Cusco in the afternoon.

Day 7: Red Valley or alternative experiences
Options according to your interests:

  • Red Valley, a hidden gem next to Vinicunca.
  • Andean Baroque Route, visiting colonial churches.
  • Cocalmayo hot springs, to relax before returning.

Recommendations according to your budget

Economical:

  • Stay in hostels or Airbnb.
  • Use public transportation or group tours.
  • Eat at local markets (San Pedro or San Blas).

Intermediate:

  • Boutique or comfortable hotels.
  • Train to Machu Picchu in tourist class.
  • Tours in small groups.

Luxury:

  • 4-5 star hotels.
  • Train Hiram Bingham to Machu Picchu.
  • Exclusive experiences such as glamping or gourmet dinners.

Always remember to book in advance and prepare your trip to have a better experience. Certain visits to attractions require booking a month in advance to have the best views and routes. Book here and now and have a unique experience.
